source.title: Region-Specific Regulation of Presynaptic Dopamine Homeostasis by D2 Autoreceptors Shapes the Impact of the Neuropsychiatric Disease-Associated DAT Variant Val559.

confidence_rationale: Mechanistic transgenic-mouse study that shows the bounding dependency AND its runaway failure mode in one system: normally D2 autoreceptors tonically constrain presynaptic DA (via DAT trafficking + tyrosine-hydroxylase control), but in the DAT Val559 variant tonic D2AR activation flips into a POSITIVE-FEEDBACK loop -- it drives surface expression of efflux-prone transporters, raising extracellular DA and 'overwhelming DAT-mediated DA clearance capacity'. That is a concrete biological instance of a homeostat losing its bound and running away -- the precise dynamical shape of the 711 blow-up (a plastic positive-feedback loop with no saturation). Direction 'mixed': it SUPPORTS the existence of the tonic homeostatic bound, but its headline is the PATHOLOGICAL runaway (a disease variant), so it also functions as the cautionary failure-signature. Confidence 0.62: strong mechanism, but a specific disease-variant model with region/sex specificity, so transfer to REE's abstract controller is via analogy of dynamics, not of substrate.
failure_signatures: A tonic drive coupled to a plastic amplifier with no saturation becomes a positive-feedback runaway that overwhelms the downstream clearance/normalization capacity (Val559: tonic D2AR -> efflux-prone DAT -> DA rises -> more efflux). REE's pre-repair ascending M_cross maturation is the same shape; the anti-windup clamp (ASG-4) is the missing saturation.

Whether a homeostatic loop BOUNDS or RUNS AWAY can depend on region-specific parameters (dorsal vs ventral striatum here) -- predicts REE's parity controller may need loop-specific (limbic vs motor) bounding constants rather than one global ceiling ratio.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Presynaptic dopamine homeostasis is set by tonic D2-autoreceptor control of DA synthesis, release and transporter-mediated clearance; when this control is perturbed (DAT Val559), tonic D2AR activation drives a positive-feedback loop that increases efflux-prone transporter surface expression, elevates extracellular DA, and overwhelms clearance capacity.
mapping.ree_translation: Concretely grounds BOTH halves of the 711 repair: (i) ASG-3 -- the tonic-DA-homeostasis loop that normally holds dopaminergic drive within a band; (ii) the failure mode -- when that loop lacks saturation it becomes a positive-feedback runaway that overwhelms the downstream normalizer, which is exactly the unbounded ascending M_cross maturation the anti-windup clamp (ASG-4) was added to stop. Shows the homeostat and its runaway are two regimes of the SAME loop, matching REE's 709(sub-threshold)->711(runaway) 'no stable operating point' finding.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a disease-variant (Val559) mouse model; the runaway is engineered by a specific transporter mutation, not a generic property of the healthy spiral. Mapping its presynaptic-efflux positive feedback onto REE's cross-loop-weight maturation is a dynamical analogy (positive feedback + no saturation -> blow-up), not a substrate correspondence.
mapping.source_context: Ex vivo + in vivo transgenic mouse (adolescent males); voltammetry + biochemistry; region-specific (dorsal vs ventral striatum).

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (J Neurosci, Blakely lab). Mapping fidelity good for the runaway-dynamics analogy; transfer risk elevated because it is a disease-variant model and the correspondence is at the level of loop dynamics, not molecular substrate.
